report:
Based on the highest-quality evidence available — large randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews — **hydroxychloroquine does not reduce the risk of dying from COVID-19**.

**Key evidence:**

- **RECOVERY trial** (UK, one of the largest RCTs, >11,000 hospitalized patients): Found no significant difference in 28-day mortality between hydroxychloroquine and standard care; the hydroxychloroquine arm was stopped early because it was clearly ineffective ([yahoo.com](https://www.yahoo.com/news/uk-halts-trial-hydroxychloroquine-covid-140017966.html); [firstpost.com](https://www.firstpost.com/health/anti-malaria-drug-hydroxychloroquine-ineffective-against-coronavirus-reveal-uk-recovery-trials-8896831.html)).

- **WHO Solidarity trial**, a large international RCT across many countries, similarly found "little or no reduction in the mortality of hospitalised COVID-19 patients" with hydroxychloroquine compared to standard of care, leading WHO to halt that arm of the trial ([who.int](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/coronavirus-disease-covid-19-hydroxychloroquine); [nejm.org](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa2023184)).

- **Cochrane systematic review**, which pools evidence from multiple high-quality RCTs, concluded plainly: "Hydroxychloroquine does not reduce deaths from COVID-19, and probably does not reduce the number of people needing mechanical ventilation" ([cochrane.org](https://www.cochrane.org/news/chloroquine-or-hydroxychloroquine-useful-treating-people-covid-19-or-preventing-infection)).

**Context:** Early enthusiasm for hydroxychloroquine came largely from small, poorly controlled observational studies. Once large, well-designed randomized trials (RECOVERY, Solidarity, and others) were completed, they consistently showed no mortality benefit, and no increased benefit for reducing ventilation needs either. Some observational studies claiming benefit (or harm) were later found to be based on flawed or fraudulent datasets, and are not considered reliable evidence.

**Conclusion:** The weight of rigorous randomized controlled trial evidence and systematic review analysis is consistent: hydroxychloroquine does **not** reduce COVID-19 mortality. Major health authorities (WHO, NIH, and others) do not recommend it for treating COVID-19.
